raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

A complete tool call can disappear when the model emits invalid JSON under `--tool-call-parser qwen` / `qwen25`. Non-streaming parsing logs the JSON error and drops the call; streaming treats it as unfinished input. The OpenAI layer can consequently report a successful stop with no tool call, leaving an agent's requested action undone.

This was found during a **synthetic OpenCode deployment experiment**, not a production-user trace.

<details>
<summary>Deployment evidence and reduced reproduction</summary>

Environment: SGLang 0.5.21, one RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition 600W, `ProCreations/Nanbeige4.3-33B-NVFP4-A16`, DFlash draft, FP8 KV cache, 524288 context limit. The selected parser was `qwen`; chat-template options included `tool_call_format="json"` and thinking enabled. Tool grammar constraints were disabled.

In the 2026-11-02 21:06 UTC synthetic test, OpenCode 2.0.30 completed two reads, performed no edit or shell check, emitted zero error events, and exited 0. The fixture assertions failed. Its second parsed response contained:

```json
{
  "content": "Both files are read. Now I'll edit `greeting.py` to implement the required behavior",
  "tool_calls": [],
  "finish_reason": "stop",
  "done": true
}
```

A **separate native-generation replay of the captured prompt** produced a complete XML-style `edit` call despite the JSON template setting. This is a separate generation, not a byte-identical capture of the parsed response above. It motivates the deterministic reproduction; it does not prove that the original generation contained exactly the same bytes.

Reduced synthetic payload, included in the tests:

```text
I'll edit the file.
<tool_call>
<function=edit>
<parameter=text>synthetic payload</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
```

With an `edit` tool declared, current upstream silently returns no call for this payload. The patch raises `ToolCallParseError`. The same behavior is checked with malformed JSON and valid JSON followed by trailing garbage, so the fix is not specific to XML or Nanbeige.

The original replay artifact has SHA-256 `d1420e8c86eba9545bd1958e51a1ed58f8ccbe50b592309f78da349b408d9447`. Only the reduced synthetic fixture and aggregate observations are shared; no deployment endpoints, credentials, or user transcripts are included.

</details>

## Modifications

- Reject JSON decoding failures only when both tool-call delimiters have arrived. Unterminated calls keep their existing truncation behavior.
- Validate streaming fragments independently of the base parser's consumable buffer. This catches trailing garbage even after valid arguments have already been emitted, without repeatedly joining the accumulated payload.
- Propagate a typed parser error through Chat Completions and Responses. Non-streaming requests return HTTP 500; Chat streams emit an error and `[DONE]`, and Responses streams emit `response.failed`, without a successful terminal event.
- Keep generated arguments out of the error message. Do not reinterpret XML, repair JSON, or change sampling/grammar settings.
- Add CPU-registered parser and API regressions, including every two-chunk split, one-character streams, mixed closing forms, literal tags and escaped quotes/backslashes inside arguments, a malformed call after a valid call, and valid/truncated controls.

Already emitted streaming deltas cannot be retracted. Clients should treat the error as a failed response; this change does not provide transactional tool execution.

Related: #26793 proposes accepting Qwen XML via a different parser. This PR instead makes a complete payload that violates the selected JSON format an explicit error. #41039 addresses flushing valid calls at stream end; this PR leaves `finish()` unchanged.

The newline-free closing-tag regression raised in [review](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47986#discussion_r4448311934) is addressed in `7cf0b005d`. The validator recognizes both supported streaming closing forms while tracking JSON string/escape state across chunks. The mixed-closing regression fails on `33f63cb` and passes with the follow-up fix.

## Accuracy Tests

No model forward pass, weights, quantization, or sampling changes. The deployment evidence predates this patch; **no GPU deployment or agent-success claim is made for the patch**.

On macOS arm64 / Python 3.12.13 (repository-pinned `tml-renderers==0.1.0`):

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/function_call/ \
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/ \
  --cov=python/sglang/srt --cov-config=.coveragerc --cov-report=xml -q
diff-cover coverage.xml --compare-branch=upstream/main --fail-under=60
```

- **1,291 tests and 3,837 subtests passed.**
- **95% changed-line coverage**, including 100% of the changed Qwen detector lines.
- The new regressions fail with unmodified upstream production files and pass after restoring the patch: **12 tests and 846 subtests passed**. Valid JSON and unterminated-block controls retain existing behavior.
- Replayed the original saved synthetic model output directly through both detector implementations: upstream returned zero calls; the patch raised `ToolCallParseError`.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed for the six changed files, including the test registry checks; `git diff --check` passed.
- **Full-repository lint passed in [upstream Linux CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41535431658), as did the PR title check.** The local macOS `pre-commit run --all-files` attempt encountered Linux-only Rust APIs and inherited a Python 3.13 formatter target from an ancestor `pyproject.toml`; the latter caused unrelated formatting changes, which were reverted. The formatter target was confirmed with Ruff's `--show-settings`. No hooks were disabled or repository checks weakened.
- Upstream test workflows have not run: their gates require a maintainer to add `run-ci`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No decode tokens/s improvement is claimed. The changed work is CPU output parsing; GPU generation and transfer are outside the measurement.

Exploratory Apple M4 Pro / Python 3.12.13 timings, rerun on `7cf0b005d`: median of 15 interleaved baseline/patched full-response parses, including detector construction and `finish()`, with GC collected before each timed sample. The baseline Qwen implementation is identical in `bde43d6c` and the rebased parent `efdcb420c`.

| Synthetic input | Stream chunk size | Baseline | Patched |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 65,538 characters of ordinary text | 16 characters | 12.008 ms | 13.089 ms |
| JSON call with a 4 KiB string argument | 16 characters | 41.731 ms | 42.520 ms |
| JSON call with a 64 KiB string argument | 64 characters | 2,638.628 ms | 2,648.162 ms |

The tool payload was `json.dumps({"name": "edit", "arguments": {"text": "x" * size}})`, enclosed in the standard Qwen tags; ordinary text was `"plain text " * 5958`. These include existing incremental-parser costs and host timing noise. They are not GPU decode benchmarks or statistical performance bounds.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit; changed-file checks pass. Full-repository limitations are recorded above.
- [x] Add unit tests using `CustomTestCase` and `register_cpu_ci`.
- [x] Documentation assessed: no new flags or model support; changed error behavior and compatibility are documented here.
- [x] Provide applicable correctness and parser timing evidence; model accuracy/decode benchmarking is not applicable.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style.

## Review and Merge Process

@slin1237 @JustinTong0323 — please review the parser/API error behavior and authorize the CPU CI suite when appropriate.

+"""Complete invalid Qwen JSON tool calls must not look like a normal stop."""
+
+import json
+import unittest
+
+from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
+from sglang.srt.function_call.function_call_parser import FunctionCallParser
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestQwen25InvalidJSON(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.tools = [
+            Tool(
+                type="function",
+                function=Function(
+                    name="edit",
+                    parameters={
+                        "type": "object",
+                        "properties": {"text": {"type": "string"}},
+                        "required": ["text"],
+                    },
+                ),
+            )
+        ]
+        # Reduced from a synthetic Nanbeige4.3 deployment reproduction:
+        # the JSON chat template was selected, but the model emitted XML.
+        self.invalid_payloads = [
+            "<function=edit>\n<parameter=text>synthetic payload</parameter>\n</function>",
+            '{"name":"edit","arguments":{"text":invalid}}',
+            '{"name":"edit","arguments":{"text":"ok"}} trailing garbage',
+        ]
+
+    def parser(self, name="qwen"):
+        return FunctionCallParser(self.tools, name)
+
+    def test_complete_invalid_block_non_streaming(self):
+        for name in ("qwen", "qwen25"):
+            for payload in self.invalid_payloads:
+                with self.subTest(parser=name, payload=payload):
+                    wire = (
+                        "I'll edit the file.\n<tool_call>\n"
+                        + payload
+                        + "\n</tool_call>"
+                    )
+                    with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "Invalid JSON") as cm:
+                        self.parser(name).parse_non_stream(wire)
+                    self.assertNotIn(payload, str(cm.exception))
+
+    def test_complete_invalid_block_streaming_at_every_split(self):
+        for end_tag in ("\n</tool_call>", "</tool_call>"):
+            for payload in self.invalid_payloads:
+                wire = "I'll edit the file.\n<tool_call>\n" + payload + end_tag
+                for split in range(len(wire) + 1):
+                    with self.subTest(end_tag=end_tag, payload=payload, split=split):
+                        parser = self.parser()
+                        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "Invalid JSON"):
+                            parser.parse_stream_chunk(wire[:split])
+                            parser.parse_stream_chunk(wire[split:])
+                            parser.parse_stream_end()
+
+    def test_streaming_calls_with_mixed_end_tags(self):
+        values = (
+            "first",
+            "literal </tool_call> inside JSON",
+            'escaped quote "</tool_call> and backslash \\',
+            'escaped newline\n</tool_call> and "quotes"',
+            r"backslash and quote \"</tool_call>",
+            r"two backslashes \\</tool_call>",
+            "many </tool_call> tags " * 8,
+        )
+        for first_end in ("</tool_call>", "\n</tool_call>"):
+            for second_end in ("</tool_call>", "\n</tool_call>"):
+                for value in values:
+                    for width in (1, 2, 7, 16, 1024):
+                        with self.subTest(
+                            first_end=first_end,
+                            second_end=second_end,
+                            value=value,
+                            width=width,
+                        ):
+                            parser = self.parser()
+                            calls = []
+                            for text, end_tag in (
+                                (value, first_end),
+                                ("second", second_end),
+                            ):
+                                for part in (
+                                    "<tool_call>\n",
+                                    '{"name":"edit",',
+                                    '"arguments":' + json.dumps({"text": text}) + "}",
+                                    end_tag,
+                                ):
+                                    for start in range(0, len(part), width):
+                                        calls.extend(
+                                            parser.parse_stream_chunk(
+                                                part[start : start + width]
+                                            )[1]
+                                        )
+                            calls.extend(parser.parse_stream_end()[1])
+                            self.assertEqual(
+                                [call.name for call in calls if call.name],
+                                ["edit", "edit"],
+                            )
+                            for index, text in enumerate((value, "second")):
+                                arguments = "".join(
+                                    call.parameters
+                                    for call in calls
+                                    if call.tool_index == index
+                                )
+                                self.assertEqual(json.loads(arguments), {"text": text})
+
+    def test_unclosed_json_string_before_standard_end_tag(self):
+        wire = (
+            '<tool_call>\n{"name":"edit","arguments":{"text":"unfinished\n</tool_call>'
+        )
+        for split in range(len(wire) + 1):
+            with self.subTest(split=split):
+                parser = self.parser()
+                with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "Invalid JSON"):
+                    parser.parse_stream_chunk(wire[:split])
+                    parser.parse_stream_chunk(wire[split:])
+
+    def test_invalid_block_after_valid_call(self):
+        valid = '<tool_call>\n{"name":"edit","arguments":{"text":"ok"}}\n</tool_call>'
+        invalid = "<tool_call>\n" + self.invalid_payloads[0] + "\n</tool_call>"
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "Invalid JSON"):
+            self.parser().parse_non_stream(valid + invalid)
+        parser = self.parser()
+        for chunk in (
+            "<tool_call>\n",
+            '{"name":"edit",',
+            '"arguments":{"text":"ok"}}',
+            "\n</tool_call>",
+        ):
+            parser.parse_stream_chunk(chunk)
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "Invalid JSON"):
+            parser.parse_stream_chunk(invalid)
+
+    def test_streaming_validation_survives_consumed_arguments(self):
+        wire = "<tool_call>\n" + self.invalid_payloads[-1] + "\n</tool_call>"
+        for width in (1, 2, 7, 16, len(wire)):
+            with self.subTest(width=width):
+                parser = self.parser()
+                with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "Invalid JSON"):
+                    for start in range(0, len(wire), width):
+                        parser.parse_stream_chunk(wire[start : start + width])
+                    parser.parse_stream_end()
+
+    def test_unterminated_block_keeps_existing_truncation_behavior(self):
+        for payload in self.invalid_payloads:
+            wire = "<tool_call>\n" + payload
+            self.parser().parse_non_stream(wire)
+            parser = self.parser()
+            for character in wire:
+                parser.parse_stream_chunk(character)
+            parser.parse_stream_end()
+
+    def test_valid_json_preserves_literal_markup_and_unicode(self):
+        value = 'before </parameter> after\n"quotes" & unicode é'
+        payload = json.dumps({"name": "edit", "arguments": {"text": value}})
+        _, calls = self.parser().parse_non_stream(
+            "<tool_call>\n" + payload + "\n</tool_call>"
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(len(calls), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(json.loads(calls[0].parameters), {"text": value})
+        parser = self.parser()
+        calls = []
+        for chunk in (
+            "<tool_call>\n",
+            '{"name":"edit",',
+            '"arguments":' + json.dumps({"text": value}) + "}",
+            "\n</tool_call>",
+        ):
+            calls.extend(parser.parse_stream_chunk(chunk)[1])
+        calls.extend(parser.parse_stream_end()[1])
+        self.assertEqual([call.name for call in calls if call.name], ["edit"])
+        self.assertEqual(
+            json.loads("".join(call.parameters for call in calls)), {"text": value}
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle the supported newline-free end tag in validation**

When a streamed Qwen call closes with `</tool_call>` immediately after its JSON (a form this detector explicitly handles via `end_token_without_newline`), this state machine waits only for `self.eot_token` (`\n</tool_call>`), so `_validation_parts` stays open. If another valid standard-form call follows, its closing tag causes the concatenation of both calls and the intervening tags to be passed to `json.loads`, producing `ToolCallParseError` and failing an otherwise valid response; the validator needs to recognize the alternate closing form while avoiding delimiter-like text inside JSON strings.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

The validator now recognizes both closing forms and carries JSON quote/escape state across chunks, so literal `</tool_call>` text inside arguments does not close the block. A standard newline-prefixed delimiter still rejects an unterminated JSON string. Scanning uses a cursor and accumulates fragments without repeatedly copying the remaining input.

Added regressions for all combinations of closing forms, character-sized chunks, escaped quotes/backslashes, repeated literal tags, and malformed calls at every two-chunk split. The tests verify both calls' argument values. Validation: 12 focused tests / 846 subtests and the full parser + OpenAI suites (1,291 tests / 3,837 subtests) pass; changed-file pre-commit checks pass.
